key_insight: OmniRay targets single-image 3D reconstruction across different camera types using composite ray fields. Its central idea is to separate overall camera projection from finer geometric variations rather than capture both with one fixed basis.
problem_solved: Monocular reconstruction models often assume a pinhole camera, causing distorted 3D geometry on fisheye and panoramic images. Existing camera-aware approaches use a single fixed basis that may inadequately represent different levels of camera geometry.
method: Use per-pixel viewing rays to represent camera geometry beyond the pinhole assumption.
Model camera geometry hierarchically, distinguishing overall projection from finer variations.
Introduce composite ray fields for camera-agnostic monocular 3D reconstruction; implementation details are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: The approach could make single-image 3D reconstruction more reliable across standard, fisheye, and panoramic imagery. This would help practitioners handle diverse camera inputs without relying on pinhole-only assumptions.
visual_elements: Standard, fisheye, and panoramic images side by side, highlighting projection differences.
Diagram of pixels mapped to viewing rays in 3D.
Conceptual decomposition of a ray field into overall projection and finer variations.
Illustrative comparison of distorted versus camera-aware reconstructed geometry, clearly labeled as conceptual.
paper_title: OmniRay: Camera-Agnostic Monocular 3D Reconstruction with Composite Ray Fields
paper_authors: Namitha Guruprasad, Abhay Yadav, Cheng Peng, Rama Chellappa, Anand Bhattad
